findings.charge: The subject carries three unrevised 'D-167' references that were forward placeholders for an unminted decision when v3 authored them, and that this very remeasurement renders stale. At live HEAD c77ff47, D-167 is an adopted decision about a different row, so the three sentences no longer mean what they were written to mean — while the same artifact treats D-167 as adopted history in three other fields.
evidence: Provenance: the three sentences first appear in leftover-join.v3, whose head is 5d5d778. At 5d5d778 the last decision in COORD is D-166, so D-167 was then the next unminted number and the sentences read as 'this join does not mint the decision that would record the G15 specification'. v4 carried them; v5 carries them unchanged.

At live HEAD, D-167 exists and is 'Add DR-G31 as required-now identity-namespace negative-test execution obligation'. Its own doesNot list includes 'Does not force a ride onto G15', so it is unrelated to harness.DR-G15.packaging-adapter-conformance.v7.

basedOn.g15v7.role now reads '... CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED. Not QUALIFIED. Not a D-167 recording.' Applied to the G15 specification at live HEAD, this denies a relationship to an unrelated adopted decision instead of stating the fact it was written to state, namely that no decision has yet recorded that specification.

obligations[OBL-G15-HARNESS-SPEC].reason closes 'This join does not execute G15 and does not record D-167.' A decision that is already adopted cannot be recorded by this join; the disclaimer is unserviceable as written.

proposedLaterWork[3] is internally inconsistent within a single entry: 'A later D-000 recording may pin that specification. Execution remains qualification. This join does not record D-167.' It names a generic future D-000 for the recording and then disclaims recording a number that is already spent on another row.

The same artifact uses D-167 with the opposite, correct referent in three places: authorityClaim 'v5 remasures after D-167/D-169/D-173', purpose 'after D-167/D-169/D-173', and remeasurementClause 'This join does not unwrite D-167 through D-173'. One clause treats D-167 as adopted history not to be unwritten while three others treat it as a future act not to be performed.
findings.whyThisMatters: OBL-G15-HARNESS-SPEC is one of the two load-bearing measurements this version exists to carry, and basedOn.g15v7.role is the custody field a coordinator reads to determine whether the G15 specification is recorded. Both now point at an adopted, unrelated decision. This is the same carry-staleness defect class the version's own purpose repairs for version numbers (CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1) — a concrete number embedded in a sentence that outlives its referent — left unrepaired for decision numbers, in the artifact whose stated job is to remasure against D-167/D-169/D-173.
findings.whyNotABlocker: No measurement is falsified. Each of the three sentences remains literally true as a negative, the obligation partition is unchanged, and no unauthorized act is performed. The defect is a drifted referent in disclaimer and role prose, not a false claim about the live register.
findings.suggestedRepairShape: Apply the same carry-safe rewrite already used for the version sentence: replace the concrete decision number with a self-describing phrase — for example 'Not recorded by any decision' in basedOn.g15v7.role, and 'does not record that specification' / 'This join does not perform that recording' in the obligation reason and proposedLaterWork[3]. This is prose-only, touches no pin, no digest, and no obligation flag, and leaves the D-167/D-169/D-173 remeasurement citations in authorityClaim, purpose, and remeasurementClause intact.
findings.notARequestTo: This finding does not ask the author to record the G15 specification, to mint a decision number, to change any obligation's leftoverDesign, or to move any pin.
